section_summary.extract_value: This section reports measurement invariance across sex for a one-dimensional model using MGCFA, finding configural, metric, and full scalar invariance. A t-test comparing total BAS-2 scores between men and women showed no significant difference (t(383) = 0.04, p = .970), with identical mean BAS-2 scores for men and women (M = 3.72) and reported SDs of 0.81 (men) and 0.73 (women).
section_summary.evidence_source: Since the one-dimensional model had an acceptable fit in both sex subsamples, MGCFA was performed (see Table 1). Differences between configural and metric model, as well as between metric and scalar model, indicated full scalar equivalence. This allowed the use of a t-test to compare mean scores for men and women. There was no significant between-group difference in total BAS-2 scores, t(383) = 0.04, p = .970, d < 0.01, M_{\text{men}} = 3.72, SD = 0.81, M_{\text{women}} = 3.72, SD = 0.73.
